title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: declarative agents ground answers in scanned PDFs from SharePoint
summary: The roadmap facts and both controls' paths and commands are supported. The statement that the sources show only licence and administration costs overlooks their documented metered-usage route, which could mislead budgeting. The licensing discussion also needs to acknowledge conflicting Microsoft guidance.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SharePoint grounding is limited to content the asking user can access.
claims.quote: When you configure your agent to use SharePoint and OneDrive content as knowledge, Copilot searches SharePoint and OneDrive files, folders, or sites that a user has access to for grounding information.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An agent's SharePoint knowledge can be scoped by URL to a site, document library, folder or file.
claims.quote: URLs should be full path to SharePoint items (site, document library, folder, or file).

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Omitting both ItemsByUrl and ItemsBySharePointIds allows access to all organisational OneDrive and SharePoint content accessible to the signed-in user.
claims.quote: If you don't specify the `ItemsByUrl` array (or the alternative `ItemsBySharePointIds` array), the agent can access all OneDrive and SharePoint content in your Microsoft 365 organization that the signed-in user can access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Agent Builder respects existing permissions and sensitivity labels on files already uploaded to SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: The agent respects existing permissions and [sensitivity labels](/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels) for files already uploaded to SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.claim: Agent Builder cannot use SharePoint knowledge when Restricted SharePoint Search is enabled.
claims.quote: If [Restricted SharePoint Search](/en-us/sharepoint/restricted-sharepoint-search) is enabled, you can't use SharePoint as a knowledge source.

claims.claim: An administrator can block an agent at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **All agents**. In the **All agents** page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select **Block** or **Unblock**.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent usage.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The admin centre Block action prevents users across the organisation from using the selected agent.
claims.quote: **Block and unblock** | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: The Graph block API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Access to the Graph Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a [Microsoft Agent 365](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365) license.

claims.claim: The Graph block endpoint takes no request body.
claims.quote: Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: Blocking agents created with Agent Builder or Copilot Studio affects their availability in Copilot and other host products.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products

claims.claim: Blocking agents created with SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry affects only Microsoft Copilot Chat availability.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The admin agent-actions page does not name agents built with Agents Toolkit in its cross-host blocking explanation.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio ... However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is configured at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand **Sites** and select **Active sites**. Select the site you want to configure. Open the **Settings** tab, and then turn **Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot** on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote:
## Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
### Use PowerShell
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires the organisation to be licensed for Copilot and have SharePoint Advanced Management available.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits site discovery in organisation-wide search and Copilot responses rather than changing permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites ... in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses ... Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery applies to SharePoint sites, not OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Users who already have permission can directly access content after Restricted Content Discovery is applied.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: The Restricted Content Discovery page does not specifically describe its effect on declarative agents whose knowledge is pinned to a SharePoint item.
claims.quote: Searched: declarative agent scanned PDF SharePoint grounding; declarative agent scanned PDF admin disable setting Graph. Read restricted-content-discovery in full: it distinguishes tenant-wide discovery from site context and content already in use, but does not specify pinned agent knowledge.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: The listed controls govern agent availability and site discovery, not a separate scanned-document-reading setting.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting. When you turn on the setting, Microsoft 365 search systems propagate it so that content from the site doesn't appear in organization-wide discovery experiences.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes answer grounding, not a new ability to perform actions.
